title: OEE Framework
body: Availability alone is lying to you right now — dump trucks and excavators sit at 90%+ mechanical availability, but utilization runs 15-25 points below that. Judge the fleet on availability only and you'll miss the real output being lost to standby time and unrecorded quality failures.
keyPoints: OEE = Availability × Performance × Quality ÷ 10,000. Three separate loss categories — a machine can be "available" all shift and still produce nothing if it's standing idle waiting for a location.
The Performance gap at ADW traces to dispatch and sequencing, not mechanics — "no location" and "waiting for excavator" are the recurring standby reasons dragging utilization below availability.
Quality losses are the blind spot: ROM pad wrong-tipping and crusher bin-starvation stoppages are true output losses, but nobody's counting them as a category yet.
The Kaizen event already proved this pattern — people and process are the constraint on this fleet, not equipment condition.
apply: Watch the standby gap at the loading face — a truck sitting on "waiting for excavator" is a Performance loss exactly like the ones dragging utilization below availability in the June data, and it's fixable with sequencing, not maintenance.
